body:
The web client has no handling for a rejected bearer token (grep: no 401
handling anywhere outside tests). After a password change on another device
(T-45 revokes other sessions), a session revoke, or any token invalidation,
the SPA stays "logged in" (account in sessionStorage) while every API call
fails — the header shows "Sync failed" forever and every screen is dead until
the user figures out they must manually log out.

Android already does this right: ErrorInterceptor fires
SessionEvents.notifyForcedLogout() on a 401 from a request that carried an
Authorization header, and the app clears local state and returns to login.

Fix: in apiFetch (web/src/api/client.ts), when a request that sent a bearer
token gets a 401 back, clear the token + stored account and send the user to
/login (preserving location state like ProtectedRoute does, so post-login
returns them where they were). Requests without a token (login/register
credential failures) must NOT trigger it — same rule as Android.

Files: web/src/api/client.ts, web/src/auth/AuthContext.tsx (+ test).
title: Web: no 401 handling — revoked token leaves the app in a dead logged-in state
